---
title: "Sparse Cox proportional hazards models"
description: "Right-censored survival data with adaptive ridge and scalable risk-set calculations."
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>", message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(L0glm)
options(width=90, digits=3)
```

The Cox model describes the hazard as

\[
h(t\mid x_i)=h_0(t)\exp(x_i^\top\beta).
\]

Use `survival::Surv(time, status)` with `mgcv::cox.ph()`. Status is one for
an observed event and zero for right censoring. The baseline hazard absorbs an
intercept, so the coefficient model has no separate intercept.

## Fit sparse survival effects

```{r fit}
set.seed(23)
X <- matrix(rnorm(400*25), 400, 25)
event <- rexp(400, exp(.9*X[, 2]-.7*X[, 9]))
censor <- rexp(400, .3)
y <- survival::Surv(pmin(event, censor), event <= censor)

fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family=mgcv::cox.ph(),
  lambda="gic", relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100, tol=1e-8)
fit
predict(fit, X[1:5, ], type="risk")
```

Risk predictions are relative hazards `exp(X %*% beta + offset)`.
The implementation uses the Breslow treatment of tied event times.

## Tune by GIC or cross-validation

```{r tuning, eval=FALSE}
gic <- L0glm.tune(X, y, family=mgcv::cox.ph(), tune="gic",
  nlambda=10, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100)
cv <- L0glm.tune(X, y, family=mgcv::cox.ph(), tune="cv",
  nfolds=5, nlambda=10, relaxed=TRUE, maxit=100)
```

Cox CV uses partial-likelihood subtraction with the full risk sets.
The [Cox help page](../reference/L0glm_cox.html) includes the likelihood,
quadratic approximation and a reproducible `glmnet` comparison based on its
[Coxnet example](https://glmnet.stanford.edu/articles/Coxnet.html).

## Scaling the quadratic updates

Event ordering and tied-risk-set bookkeeping are cached. Small dense active
systems use Cholesky LLT. Larger systems use matrix-free preconditioned conjugate
gradients: Hessian-vector products avoid constructing the full predictor Hessian.
The initializer also has a matrix-free ridge path. Control these choices through
`control.family`; the default selects an appropriate path automatically.

Broken adaptive ridge for scalable Cox regression is developed by
[Kawaguchi et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.8438).
The [algorithm article](algorithm.html) explains how the package combines
quadratic likelihood updates with adaptive penalties.
